messages:
Maya: Quick sync — proposal for dynamic throttling tied to billing usage. Goal: prevent noisy spikes from small customers while letting paid customers burst. Need to agree PRD acceptance criteria + edge cases. TL;DR: per-account baseline quota + burst pool that charges at a higher rate.

Sam: sounds good. can you list the concrete acceptance checks we need before launch? e.g., API behavior on over-limit, metrics to validate, and roll-out plan.

Maya: yes — initial checklist suggestion: 1) API semantics defined (429 vs 402), 2) server-side meter emits per-request meter events with cost labels, 3) UI shows realtime quota & burst consumption, 4) experiment on 10% of traffic for 2 weeks, compare latency and $/req.

Jordan: important: we must separate "throttle" from "charge" signals. If we return 429 we should not bill for that token. If we allow burst and bill, we return 200 but include X-Burst-Charge header. Otherwise disputes will explode.

Lee: design question — how visible should burst charges be in console? My recommendation: two lines in usage: "Committed quota" and "Burst usage (metered at premium)" with tooltip. Also add in-app notification when burst > 50% of baseline for 24h.

Sam: edge cases I care about: 1) multi-tenant keys (org-level vs project-level), 2) streaming responses where per-token billing vs per-request throttle interacts, 3) retries/backoffs — clients may hammer after 429. We should include Retry-After and a suggested exponential backoff guide in docs.

Maya: good. For API semantics proposal:
```
- 200: request served normally. Response headers: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Burst-Used (tokens).
- 402: request would have exceeded billable burst and account has insufficient balance/entitlement. Body explains next steps.
- 429: request denied due to rate limit at baseline. Retry-After header provided.
```
This differentiates billing rejection vs transient throttling. Thoughts?

Jordan: +1 on 402 for bill-blocked flows. Implementation note: many customers pay post-pay — for them 402 should map to billing hold state. We need a webhook so customers can auto-top-up before we 402 them.

Sam: implementation feasibility: runtime can emit a "charge-intent" event during scheduling. If charge succeeds, continue; if billing check fails, short-circuit with 402. For streaming we need to preauthorize estimated tokens for long streams — else we risk mid-stream 402. That's messy. Maybe cap streaming sessions at a preauthorized token limit.

Lee: UI acceptance criteria: show preauthorized stream tokens in the session modal and an inline CTA to purchase more burst capacity. Also design a lightweight banner for 402 so customers know it's billing, not a bug.

Maya: rollout plan: implement server + billing hooks in 1.0, soft-launch to 5 customers (who opt in), 2-week experiment 10% of API traffic, then ramp. Acceptance metrics: false-402 rate < 0.5% (billing disputes), average burst revenue lift >= 8% for opted customers, no >2% increase in 95p latency.

Sam: tests I'll add: unit tests for header semantics, e2e sim with streaming preauth and mid-stream fail, chaos test where billing API is slow and we exercise fallback to baseline-only mode.

Jordan: add CLAUSE: customers on Enterprise with contract overrides should not be auto-402'd. We need customer-level overrides in DB and a UI toggle for billing ops.

Maya: noted. Next steps: Sam to draft API spec + error payloads, Jordan to write billing webhook contract, Lee to mock UI banner + quota view, I'll assemble PRD and acceptance checklist. Can we have first drafts by EOD Wednesday?

Sam: yes — will post API spec draft in this thread.

Lee: I'll upload mock PNGs to the design board and link here when ready. :+1:

ops-bot: deploy-notify: integration-test job started for feature/charge-intent (build 472).

Maya: thanks everyone — putting this in the PRD queue. Keeping thread for spec reviews. :sparkles:
